[[File:Logo - Young African Leaders Initiative.JPG|thumb|YALI logo]]
The '''Young African Leaders Initiative''' ('''YALI''') is an [[Popular initiative|initiative]] of the [[United States Department of State]]. It was started by President [[Barack Obama]] in 2010. YALI is a programme aimed at educating and networking young [[Africa]]n leaders with activities including the '''Mandela Washington Fellowship''' that brings them to study in the United States for six weeks with follow-up resources and student exchange programs.<ref name="state">{{cite web|url=https://youngafricanleaders.state.gov/yali-africa/|title=YALI and Africa|publisher=Young African Leaders Initiative|access-date=August 12, 2014|archive-date=March 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160313230321/https://youngafricanleaders.state.gov/yali-africa/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2014, the program was expanded to include four regional "leadership centers" in [[Ghana]], [[Kenya]], [[Senegal]] and [[South Africa]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2014/07/28/background-fact-sheet-president-s-young-african-leaders-initiative-yali|title=BACKGROUND & FACT SHEET: The President’s Young African Leaders Initiative (YALI)|publisher=White House Office of the Press|date=July 28, 2014}}</ref><ref name="mandela">{{cite web |title=Mandela Washington Fellowship |url=https://yali.state.gov/mwf/ |website=Young African Leaders Initiative |publisher=US Department of State |access-date= November 11, 2019}}</ref>

500 participants in the Mandela Washington Fellowship arrived in the United States on June 16, 2014.<ref name="The Washington Post - 16 June 2014 - U.Va. hosts Young African Leaders Initiative">{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/uva-hosts-young-african-leaders-initiative/2014/06/16/7148750c-f51c-11e3-8ac4-8c205d7d440f_story.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140622114132/http://www.washingtonpost.com/local/uva-hosts-young-african-leaders-initiative/2014/06/16/7148750c-f51c-11e3-8ac4-8c205d7d440f_story.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 22, 2014|title=U.Va. hosts Young African Leaders Initiative|agency=Associated Press|date=June 16, 2014|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date= June 22, 2014}}</ref> In 2019, there were 700 fellows.<ref name=mandela />The Mandela Washington Fellowship will not take place in 2026.  The Fellowship will continue to offer opportunities for Alumni. 

== YALI Regional Leadership Center ==
[[File:Building youth leaders, East Africa (24768121237).jpg|thumb|2017]]
As part of efforts to decentralize and to reach a large number of young leaders, the Young African Leaders Initiative program created regional leadership centers across the African continent known as the YALI Regional Leadership Center (RLC).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://yali.state.gov/rlc/|title=Regional Leadership Centers {{!}} Young African Leaders Initiative Network|work=Young African Leaders Initiative Network|access-date=March 17, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> Participants of the Regional Leadership Centers go through online and in-person training and are provided with professional development opportunities in these three track areas: Business and Entrepreneurship, Civil Society Management, and Public Policy and Management.

The Regional Leadership Center is located in [[West Africa]], with centers in the [[Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration]] (GIMPA), [[Accra]], Ghana,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://yaliwestafrica.net/rlc/|title=YALI RLC West Africa|website=YALI RLC West Africa|language=en-US|access-date=March 17, 2018|archive-date=March 8, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230308215245/http://yaliwestafrica.net/rlc/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the Centre Africain d'Etudes Supérieures en Gestion (CESAG), [[Dakar]], Senegal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.yaliafriquedelouest.org/|title=YALI WEST AFRICA REGIONAL LEADERSHIP CENTER - DAKAR|last=mElimu.com|first=mElimu {{!}}|website=www.yaliafriquedelouest.org|language=en|access-date=March 17, 2018}}</ref> The Accra Center has a satellite campus at the [[Administrative Staff College of Nigeria]] (ASCON), near [[Lagos]], Nigeria. The center in Dakar, Senegal, is for French-speaking West Africans.

There is a YALI Regional Leadership Center for East Africans located at [[Kenyatta University]], [[Nairobi]], [[Kenya]], which serves citizens of the following countries: [[Burundi]], [[Central African Republic]], [[Republic of the Congo|Republic of Congo]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], [[Djibouti]], [[Eritrea]], [[Ethiopia]], [[Kenya]], [[Rwanda]], [[Somalia]], [[South Sudan]], [[Sudan]], [[Tanzania]] and [[Uganda]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yalieastafrica.org/|title=YALI EAST AFRICA REGIONAL LEADERSHIP CENTER|last=mElimu.com|first=mElimu {{!}}|website=www.yalieastafrica.org|language=en|access-date=March 17, 2018}}</ref>

The Southern African Regional Leadership Center is at [[University of South Africa]] (UNISA) School of Business Leadership (SBL), near [[Pretoria]], South Africa, with a satellite campus at [[Eduardo Mondlane University|Universidade Eduardo Mondlane]], [[Maputo]], [[Mozambique]], for Portuguese speakers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://yalisouthernafrica.melimu.com/|title=YALI SOUTHERN AFRICA REGIONAL LEADERSHIP CENTER|last=mElimu.com|first=mElimu {{!}}|website=yalisouthernafrica.melimu.com|language=en|access-date=March 17, 2018}}</ref> 

== YALI Rwanda chapter ==
YALI Regional leadership centre East Africa Alumni has a chapter in [[Rwanda]], the mission of which is "to empower young leaders in Rwanda and East Africa to develop the skills, knowledge, and networks needed to drive sustainable development and social change."<ref>[https://yalirwandachapter.org/about/#:~:text=Our%20mission%20is%20to%20empower,next%20generation%20of%20African%20leaders. "What is YALI | About YALI RLC EA Rwanda Chapter"], https://yalirwandachapter.org/.]</ref>
